verses.text: After Ahab died, the land of Moab rebelled against Israel.

Ahaziah fell through the lattice window of his upstairs room in Samaria and was badly hurt. So he sent messengers and told them, "Go and ask Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will get better from this injury."

But the LORD's angel said to Elijah from Tishbe, "Get up and go meet the messengers of the king of Samaria. Ask them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to ask Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron?
So this is what the LORD says: You will never get up from the bed you are lying on. You will surely die.'" So Elijah went.
When the messengers came back to the king, he asked them, "Why have you come back?"

They said, "A man came to meet us. He told us, 'Go back to the king who sent you and tell him, "This is what the LORD says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending men to ask Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron? So you will never get up from the bed you are lying on. You will surely die."'"
The king asked them, "What did the man look like who came to meet you and told you this?"
They answered, "He was a hairy man, with a leather belt around his waist." The king said, "That was Elijah from Tishbe."
Then the king sent an army captain with his fifty men to Elijah. The captain went up to Elijah, who was sitting on top of a hill, and said, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down!'"
Elijah answered the captain, "If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and burn up you and your fifty men!" Then fire came down from heaven and burned up the captain and his fifty men.
The king sent another captain with his fifty men. This captain said to Elijah, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down at once!'"
Elijah answered, "If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and burn up you and your fifty men!" Then God's fire came down from heaven and burned up the captain and his fifty men.

The king sent a third captain with his fifty men. This third captain went up and fell on his knees in front of Elijah. He begged him, "Man of God, please value my life and the lives of these fifty men, your servants.
Fire came down from heaven and burned up the first two captains and their men. But now, please value my life."
The LORD's angel said to Elijah, "Go down with him. Do not be afraid of him." So Elijah got up and went down with him to the king.

Elijah told the king, "This is what the LORD says: 'You sent messengers to ask Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron. Is it because there is no God in Israel to ask? Because you did this, you will never get up from the bed you are lying on. You will surely die.'"
So Ahaziah died, just as the LORD had said through Elijah. Because Ahaziah had no son, Joram became king after him. This was in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
The rest of what Ahaziah did is written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
